source.title: On some open problems of applied automaton theory and graph theory (suggested by the mathematical modelling of certain neuronal networks)

needs_review.question_text_raw: Problem 1 asks for a structural description of all graphs satisfying the source's condition alpha.
Problem 2 asks for a structural description of all graphs satisfying the source's combined alpha-gamma condition.
Problem 3 asks whether there exists a finite strongly connected directed graph in which every two cycles have a common vertex but which fails the source's epsilon condition.
Problem 4 is referenced by the source but its full statement was not recovered from the available readable snippets.
Problem 5 asks for a method that surveys all distinct systems obtained from special permutations of the vertex set of a graph written in the source's notation G(n; m1, m2, ..., mk).
Problem 6 asks whether the family of beta-graphs is a decomposition class.
Problem 7 asks for broad decomposition classes among finite directed graphs.
Problem 8 asks for the structure of all cyclically simple directed graphs, where a cyclically simple graph is one in which the intersection of any two distinct cycles is empty or a path.
Problem 9 asks how periodicity properties are modified when some of conditions (i)-(vii) in the source's autonomous-continuous-automaton setup are weakened.
Problem 10 asks for closed formulae, as far as possible, expressing entries of a matrix associated with the network dynamics in terms of entries of the preceding row.
Problem 11 asks for a description of a network's periodicity properties, from an arbitrary initial state, using the matrix introduced in the source.

Problem 12 asks for a characterization of graphs whose associated networks have the stability property that any two periodic or pre-periodic states eventually reach a common state value at suitable times.
Problem 13 was not recovered from the available readable snippets.
Problem 14 asks whether there exists a properly periodic non-regular state of a network in the source's specified network class.
Problem 15 asks, for network classes corresponding to graph types discussed earlier in the paper, to determine the sets of periodic states and other periodicity properties.
Problem 16 asks for the study of the function n(r, s), defined through independence statements about propagation in networks with red and green directed edges.
Problem 17 asks for the study of complex networks built over graphs of the form G(n; Hp, Hq), in a manner analogous to an earlier cited investigation.
Problem 18 asks for a stochastic analogue of the network investigations when the recovery time is chosen randomly from a lognormal distribution.
Problem 19 asks which typical graph structures arise when one starts with a complete graph on n vertices and repeatedly applies the source's edge-destroying principle until k edges have been deleted.

trace.notes: Normalized the input URL as a zbMATH resolver record with trailing identifier 3583724.

Local curl attempts failed because DNS resolution is unavailable in the shell environment. Exact-title recovery found the same work in the Acta Cybernetica archive and identified a direct PDF as the primary source.

The source is a 1977 Acta Cybernetica article with chapters on graph classes, periodicity of autonomous continuous automata and networks, stochastic behaviour of networks, and stochastic genesis of networks. The available tool path exposed searchable snippets but not a locally readable full PDF text.

Recovered candidates q_001 through q_008 from the graph-theoretic chapter, but several rely on definitions of alpha, beta, gamma, special permutations, or G(n; m1, ..., mk) not fully recovered from the readable evidence.

Recovered candidates q_009 through q_017 from the periodicity and network-dynamics chapters, but several depend on source conditions, matrices, or cited network classes not fully recovered from the readable evidence.
Recovered candidates q_018 and q_019 from the stochastic-network chapter and final section.

Moved all recovered candidates to needs_review because complete, quote-grade local evidence was unavailable and accepting rewritten questions would either leave source-specific terminology undefined or rely on incomplete evidence.
Saved JSON to outputs/parse-paper/3583724.json and outputs/latest.json.
